description:
FILED s473t6b (Opus, 2026-09-17) by #1501 round 9.

PERL: `%n` in a sprintf/printf format is not output -- it STORES the number of
characters written so far into the corresponding ARGUMENT, which must be a
modifiable scalar.  perl restricts it (the argument may not come from a string
eval or an external format), and `sprintf "abc%n", $n` leaves "abc" with
$n == 3.

PCL: `%n` is not implemented.  The directive is copied to the output
LITERALLY and the argument is untouched.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL, probes/p3.pl H4):

    my $n;
    my $r = sprintf "abc%n", $n;
    printf "res=[%s] n=%s\n", $r, (defined $n ? $n : 'undef');

    perl: res=[abc] n=3
    PCL:  res=[abc%n] n=undef

ROWS: baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv
  op/sprintf.t  271 `>%n 1< Slight sneakiness to test %n`
                272 `> a1c< %n w/magic`
                273 `>1< Unicode %n`
  op/sprintf2.t 1604 `%n`
  and op/sprintf2.t's three `offset â¦` rows (1701 `reasonable result`,
  1702 `offset at start`, 1703 `offset after 1`) are the same directive read
  through `$^A`/formline's counter -- verify before closing.

SHAPE: NEW MECHANISM.  `p-sprintf` receives VALUES, not places, so it cannot
write back.  The argument would have to reach it as a cell -- the same problem
the 4-arg `substr` target and `open my $fh` already solve at the EMISSION
level (codegen marks the slot as a place), so the fix is an emission rule for
sprintf/printf whose format literal contains `%n`, not a runtime change.  A
format built at RUNTIME cannot be decided that way, and perl refuses exactly
that case ("Modification of a read-only value attempted" / its own vector
restriction), so a ruled refusal there is perl-shaped.

Low value (4-7 rows) but it is a clean emission rule; do NOT implement it by
making every sprintf argument a place.
subject: sprintf/printf %n is copied to the output LITERALLY and its argument is untouched; perl stores the characters-written count into it (4-7 rows in op/sprintf.t + op/sprintf2.t) -- an EMISSION rule (the argument has to arrive as a place), not a runtime change
